method_notes: These are LINK records only. No video, audio or thumbnail file was downloaded; every record points at Bob Zybach / ORWWmedia public originals on YouTube.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id> returned HTTP 302 -> google.com/sorry (HTTP 429, bot check) from this host, so ytInitialPlayerResponse could not be scraped.
https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player returned playabilityStatus=LOGIN_REQUIRED ("Sign in to confirm you are not a bot"), so videoDetails.shortDescription/lengthSeconds were unavailable.

WORKING endpoint: POST https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/next (InnerTube WEB client, public key) -> videoSecondaryInfoRenderer.attributedDescription.content = the full verbatim description; videoPrimaryInfoRenderer.title/dateText = title and publish date. One request per video, 1.2 s apart.

WORKING endpoint: POST https://www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/browse (browseId=VL<playlistId>) -> 19 lockupViewModel entries = playlist order, titles and duration badges; length_seconds is derived from the duration badge (hh:mm:ss), not from lengthSeconds.

https://www.youtube.com/oembed?...&format=json and https://noembed.com/embed?url=... both returned HTTP 200 with titles (verified as a cross-check on video 1); not needed as a fallback because next/ succeeded for all 19.

Segments: every description line beginning with a (hh:)mm:ss timecode. t_seconds is taken from the description link's own watchEndpoint.startTimeSeconds where YouTube linkified the timecode (authoritative), else computed from the label. label is the remainder of the line verbatim. stop_number is set when the label carries "Stop #N".

YouTube truncates long URLs in description text to "...". Real targets were recovered from attributedDescription.commandRuns urlEndpoint redirect q= parameters; description stays verbatim as displayed, description_expanded_links carries the same text with truncated URLs restored.

videos.title: 2021 Elliott Lab #1: Forest History (SWOCC F251)
videos.description:
INDEX: Elliott State Forest History with Jerry Phillips & David Gould (1 hr., 35 min., 35 sec.)

This is the history of the Elliott State Forest as told by the Elliott's two foremost historians, Jerry Phillips and David Gould. It has been prepared as the opening "distance learning" video for the 2021 Southwestern Oregon Community College (SWOCC) F251 Forest Recreation class by Dr. Bob Zybach, Oregon Websites & Watersheds Project, Inc. (ORWW), and McKenzie Peters, NW Maps Co. This program was videotaped on January 23, 2021 at Jerry's residence and features recreation of a 30-slide presentation on Elliott history he gave to the Coos District of the Oregon Department of Forestry in 2019. All of the slides were taken directly from his comprehensive 1996 history of the Elliott, "Caulked Boots & Cheese Sandwiches." David's family settled in the heart of present-day Elliott in the 1880s and have lived nearby ever since. Their extensive collection of maps, photographs, and diaries related to Elliott history stretch back to the 1880s, are largely available online through ORWW, and were developed into a book, "The Goulds of Elkhorn" -- which is also available online (link below).  

ORWW Elliott History Link: http://www.orww.org/Elliott_Forest/Hi...
Elliott Forest History (Phillips 1996): http://www.orww.org/Elliott_Forest/Hi...

videos.title: 2021 Elliott Lab #2: Recreation Planning, Monitoring and Maintenance (SWOCC F251)
videos.description:
INDEX TO VIDEO (1 hr., 41 min., 11 sec.)
This is the second student lab for the 2021 Southwestern Oregon Community College (SWOCC) F251 Forest Recreation class that is focused on the Elliott State Forest, its management, maintenance, and recreational opportunities. This lab is primarily based on the five "virtual" Elliott field trips conducted in 2020 and on the recommendations of the 2018 and 2019 SWOCC F251 Draft Elliott Recreation Plans. This lab is organized into six parts: 1) Dr. Bob Zybach briefly shows how to navigate the ORWW (Oregon Websites & Watersheds project, Inc.) Elliott websites developed by the 2018, 2019 and 2020 SWOCC F251 students; 2) McKenzie Peters, NW Maps Co. videographer, provides brief overviews and navigational directions for visiting the five Elliott field trips on the ORWWmedia YouTube channel; 3) Frank Mahoney, Portland-based videographer, and Bob show how video drones can be used to monitor and document forest roads, trails, and streams; 4) David Gould demonstrates how Elliott rock roads and historical trails can be efficiently maintained; 5) David documents several locations in the Elliott in which landslides have directly resulted in spawning gravel for anadromous fish; 6) Jerry Phillips relates the history of Jerry Phillips Reserve.

videos.title: 2020 ELLIOTT FIELD TRIP #4: Tenmile Lakes, April 29, 2020
videos.description:
INDEX TO VIDEO (47 min., 11 sec.)
This "virtual" field trip is based on detailed on-site oral history interviews with Jerry Phillips and David Gould in 2017. This route was successfully followed by the Southwestern Oregon Community College (SWOCC) 2018 and 2019 spring term F251 Forest Recreation classes. Due to coronavirus restrictions the field trips for the 2020 F251 class were videotaped and these files are also being used for the 2021 class for the same reason -- "social distancing" and "distance learning."

The 2020 Tenmile Lakes field trip is a slightly different route than that taken by the 2018 and 2019 F251 students. Guides are Jerry Phillips and David Gould and the trip begins at the site of the old Elkside Lumber Co., which has been transformed into a County Park. From there we follow the old CCC route to the isolated School Land Bay parcel and then enter the Elliott by way of Benson Ridge Road. The remainder of the field trip visits a number of cabin sites claimed by Gould family members in the early 1900s, followed by a stop at Big Saddle and finish at Jerry Phillips Reserve.  These "virtual" field trips are hosted by Dr. Bob Zybach and videotaped by McKenzie Peters, NW Maps Co.

videos.title: 2020 ELLIOTT FIELD TRIP #5: Golden & Silver Falls, May 21, 2020
videos.description:
INDEX TO VIDEO (1 hr., 10 min. 49 sec.)
This "virtual" field trip is based on detailed on-site oral history interviews with Jerry Phillips and David Gould in 2017. This route was successfully followed by the Southwestern Oregon Community College (SWOCC) 2018 and 2019 spring term F251 Forest Recreation classes. Due to coronavirus restrictions the field trips for the 2020 F251 class were videotaped and these files are also being used, with indexes and closed captioning, for the 2021 class for the same reason -- "social distancing" and "distance learning."

The Golden and Silver Falls Field Trip begins in Allegany, at the old steamboat landing from the late 1800s. We then visit riverboat historian, Roger Ott, at his home to view historic riverboat pictures on the Coos River on his computer. From Roger's home we traveled up the East Fork Millicoma River with David Gould and local logging historian, Lionel Youst. From the old logging camp at the mouth of Glenn Creek we then went to Golden and Silver Falls Park, hiking along the old Glenn Creek County Road from the base of Silver Falls to the top of Golden Falls. These "virtual" field trips are hosted by ORWW Program Manager, Dr. Bob Zybach, and videotaped by McKenzie Peters, NW Maps Co.

The host for this series has been Dr. Bob Zybach, Program Manager for Oregon Websites & Watersheds Project, Inc., and the series videographer has been McKenzie Peters, NW Maps Co. The purpose of these videos is to provide Oregon students and others with an interest in learning more about forestry and forest recreation in general -- and the Elliott State Forest in particular. videos.title: 2020 ELLIOTT WORKSHOP #1: SWOCC Distance Learning & The Elliott, April 12, 2020
videos.description:
INDEX TO VIDEO (39 min., 35 sec.)
This first "distance learning" workshop was necessitated by sudden statewide regulations in response to the 2020 coronavirus epidemic. Attempting to conduct student workshops without students, no budget, and no access to normal computer repair shops, studios, equipment rentals, or technical consultants proved problematic. Prior to the pandemic, the plan had been to focus on the history, maintenance, and potential recreational uses of the Elliott's road and trail networks, building from two successful previous years with Southwestern Oregon Community College (SWOCC) F251 Forest Recreation classes. The five established field trips and three 4-hour workshops at the SWOCC computer lab were scheduled in early March, 2020; before classroom attendance and field trips were abruptly canceled. This video marks the first attempt to transition under these conditions; from long-practiced traditional teaching methods to untested "distance learning" opportunities and constraints. Internet documentation and communications remain a common tie.  

ORWW WORKSHOP #1 LINK: http://www.orww.org/Elliott_Forest/Re...

videos.title: 2020 ELLIOTT WORKSHOP #2: Historic Roads & Trails, May 5, 2020
videos.description:
INDEX TO VIDEO (40 min. 35 sec.) 

This is the second "distance learning" Workshop for the 2020 SWOCC spring-term F251 Forest Recreation class, due to the ongoing pandemic. Two of the original nine students signing up for the course quit after the first Workshop, so topics and research assignments have changed. Conducting educational field trips and working on group projects under these circumstances has proven problematic, but remaining students seemed resilient and determined, so this has been an interesting experience. This Workshop focused on report outlines and sources of information for the reassigned student research topics, citations, and recommendations; Section 106 and SHPO "tests of significance"; digital documentation; and possible methods for improving future "virtual" field trips.

This is the third and final 2020 SWOCC F251 Forest Recreation "distance learning" Workshop resulting from the ongoing coronavirus pandemic. This Workshop is a brief review of the two earlier Workshops and five "Virtual" Field Trips in relation to the student reports. The first drafts of the reports are also briefly reviewed, with suggestions for improvements. 

[June 20, 2021 Update: Two more F251 students dropped out after the second Workshop, so it was left to only five students to complete the project, which had originally been designed for nine, and with actual meetings. This high dropout rate was certainly tied to difficulties caused by the abrupt and unanticipated changes related to the pandemic. Despite these circumstances, the remaining five students were able to complete the study and their reports, which can be found online in both HTML and PDF formats: http://www.orww.org/Elliott_Forest/Re...]

videos.title: The Ballad of Jerry Phillips
videos.description:
This message contains information about writing and recording songs about Jerry Phillips.

Bob provided the inspiration and three lines of possible lyrics. Then I took public information about Jerry Phillips and fed it into ChatGPT to create a rough draft set of lyrics ... then I edited it .. then I ported the lyrics to Suno AI and I recorded four versions ... and I sent the best one of these to Bob. I have attached this early version which is titled: Jerry's Reserve: The Heart of the Elliott. All this work took about 30 minutes.

Because Bob liked the first version, I decided to do a more professional job. So, I fed more information into ChatGPT, asked for new lyrics, spent more time editing, ported the lyrics to Suno AI and recorded about twenty versions. I have attached the best of these versions titled: The Ballad of Jerry Phillips and the Elliott State Forest.

videos.title: The Elliott: Requiem for a Boondoggle
videos.description:
INDEXED. In 1996 Wayne Giesy and I cofounded Oregon Websites & Watersheds Project, Inc., (ORWW.org)  a 501 c(3) nonprofit educational website focused on the management of Oregon's natural and cultural resources. In 2008 we launched the ORWWmedia YouTube channel, and in 2016 we began to work with local community college forestry students in studies of the Elliott State Forest. In all of those years, encompassing more than 40 educational projects, we made it a point to avoid politics and stick to facts, until now. 

This 50-minute video was sponsored by NW Maps Co., a private business, rather than ORWW because it contains political opinions regarding the Elliott and its management. The presentation was made to the CG 912 Committee in Cottage Grove, Oregon on February 6, 2024. Individual slides can be examined in more detail in the PDF version of this presentation: http://nwmapsco.com/ZybachB/Presentat...
-- Bob Zybach, Creswell, Oregon, April 28, 2024
